text: We included 5,079 individuals aged 15–24 years. The weighted national prevalence was 1.70% (95%CI = 1.31–2.08) for potential depression, 1.59% (95%CI = 1.23–1.96) for potential anxiety, and 0.96% (95%CI = 0.65–1.27) for potential suicidality among the population aged 15–24 years. In adjusted analyses, female sex was the strongest predictor of both potential depression (adjusted risk ratio [aRR] = 2.72, 95%CI = 1.55–4.79) and anxiety (aRR = 2.80, 95%CI = 1.58–4.96). Non-Kazakh ethnicity was also significantly associated with an increased risk of depression (aRR = 1.88, 95%CI = 1.17–3.02) and anxiety (aRR = 1.99, 95%CI = 1.28–3.11). PAFs indicated that female sex accounted for 45.6% and 46.8% of the risk for depression and anxiety, respectively. No significant sociodemographic correlates were identified for suicidality.
source_label: National prevalence and sociodemographic correlates of potential depression, anxiety, and suicidality among the young population in Kazakhstan: a national population-based study
